claim_ceiling: Literature-reported metrics and public dataset metadata only. None of the model results below has been independently reproduced by this project. Results on different engines, datasets, label sets, source domains and split protocols are not directly comparable.

baselines.title: A universal transfer learning framework for cross-working-condition marine diesel engine fault diagnosis based on fine-tuning strategy
baselines.data_domain: Two marine diesel engine case studies: an 8V396SE engine (500 kW) and a 620 V16 engine (2336 kW); lubrication-system fault data include experimental bench evidence and intake/exhaust fault data include virtual simulation.
baselines.task: Cross-working-condition fault diagnosis using data-tiered fusion augmentation and combined fine-tuning across 18 transfer tasks.

reported_metrics.context: The article reports validation over 18 cross-working-condition tasks; this is a protocol coverage count, not a performance score.

Abstract-reported accuracy for the paper's own cross-working-condition marine-engine task. Not reproduced here; do not treat as a common-protocol or physical fleet-transfer score. Recover the exact per-task table, class balance and split manifest before reproduction.

baselines.split_protocol: Cross-working-condition transfer across two engine types and two subsystem task families; exact source/target task definitions, per-task sample grouping and split manifests require full-methods audit.
reported_limitations: The two engine types, subsystems and mixture of experimental/virtual evidence must be kept distinct.
The accessible abstract reports the task count but no single aggregate metric suitable for direct comparison.
Not directly comparable to Aalto MU323DGSC without fault taxonomy and sensor protocol alignment.
The accessible abstract reports 95% accuracy but this is not an independently reproduced result; determine which of the 18 transfer tasks and source/target groups the score aggregates.
audit_notes: Methods include data-tiered fusion (DTF) for augmentation and a combined fine-tuning strategy (CFTS).
Use as a reproduction baseline for cross-working-condition methodology and task coverage, not as a leaderboard entry.

baselines.title: Mean value model-assisted dual transfer: a cross-domain fault diagnosis framework in diesel engines from simulation domains to experimental domains
baselines.data_domain: Simulation-assisted and experimental diesel-engine lubrication-system data; the methods describe a 16V396 simulation domain and measured 8V396 bench domain, with operating points at 70%, 85% and 100% load. This is not the Aalto MU323DGSC dataset.
baselines.task: Cross-domain lubricating-oil fault diagnosis using a mean-value-engine-model-assisted dual-transfer approach that combines data-level transfer and neural model-level transfer.

reported_metrics.context: Authors report average accuracy above 97.70% for their own cross-domain lubrication fault-diagnosis evaluation. This is literature-reported, not reproduced here; per-task composition and exact grouping must be audited before comparison.

baselines.split_protocol: Cross-domain simulation-to-experimental evaluation between 16V396 simulation and 8V396 measured bench data; the paper describes nine transfer tasks and load points 70%, 85% and 100%. Exact source/target task assignments, sample grouping, split boundaries and whether any task shares engine-specific operating trajectories require full-methods/table audit.
reported_limitations: The task is lubrication-system fault diagnosis, not the five Aalto fault families; direct score comparison is invalid.
The evaluation is cross-domain simulation-to-bench, not multi-vessel shipboard validation.
The reported >97.70% average accuracy must be decomposed by task, engine, fault class and direction; do not compare it with an aggregate from a different paper.
Code, training data, preprocessing, exact split manifests and leakage controls have not been independently audited by this project.
audit_notes: Method combines mean-value model-assisted data-level transfer with a neural model-level transfer stage.
A useful reproduction baseline for simulation-to-measured transfer and model-assisted domain adaptation.
Benchmark against source-only, target-only, fine-tuning, DANN, adaptive multi-source weighting and a calibrated non-neural baseline under exactly matched task groups.

baselines.title: Localized anomaly detection and recovery of marine engine data to support digital twin development in shipping
baselines.data_domain: Operational dataset from an ocean-going vessel; the accessible abstract describes seven operating regions and steady/transient operating modes.
baselines.task: Data quality qualification: localized anomaly identification, missing-value recovery and operating-region separation for marine-engine digital-twin development.

reported_metrics.context: The paper reports capturing seven operating regions using a GMM-EM approach; this is a dataset/model configuration fact, not a diagnostic accuracy score.
No numerical detection or recovery metric is transcribed from the accessible abstract. Full paper and data protocol must be audited.

baselines.split_protocol: Selected-vessel operating regions are modeled using GMM-EM, with localized SVD-based anomaly detection and missing-value recovery. Exact vessel identity, campaign split, data availability, labels and validation protocol require full-paper audit.
reported_limitations: Accessible abstract does not provide numerical anomaly-detection or imputation metrics.
Missing-value recovery can erase sensor-failure or anomaly evidence if imputed values are not separately typed and attributed.
Data rights, exact dataset, vessel/engine identity and independent validation have not been audited by this project.
audit_notes: Reports steady-state and transient operating-mode identification alongside GMM-EM partitioning and SVD-based recovery.
Important comparator for data-quality handling, not a directly comparable fault classifier.
Use missingness mask, imputation lineage and uncertainty as first-class benchmark outputs.

baselines.title: Hybrid AI-driven condition monitoring and RUL forecasting for multi-fault diagnosis in two-stroke marine diesel engines
baselines.data_domain: Low-speed two-stroke marine diesel engine testbed; the article reports load-aware experimental validation.
baselines.task: Integrated anomaly detection, unsupervised fault clustering, context-aware fault classification and calibrated remaining-useful-life (RUL) forecasting.

reported_metrics.context: The abstract reports representative RUL predictions with RMSE 0.215; the exact target scaling and horizon must be extracted from full methods before replication.
The abstract reports representative RUL predictions with R² 0.413.
The paper highlights consensus-based anomaly voting with false positives below 1%; denominator, operating exposure, thresholding, and confidence interval require full-protocol audit.

baselines.split_protocol: Low-speed two-stroke testbed; ensemble consensus anomaly detection; unsupervised fault clustering and labeling; load-aware supervised classification; PCA/autoencoder health-index RUL forecasting with Monte Carlo dropout. Full run-level split and RUL ground-truth construction require audit.
reported_limitations: The below-1% false-positive highlight is not interpretable as a fleet false-alarm rate without denominator and engine-hour exposure.
RUL RMSE 0.215 is paper-scale dependent; target normalization and forecast horizon are not transcribed from accessible abstract.
RUL validation without run-to-failure data must be assessed for pseudo-label/health-index leakage and calibration.
A two-stroke low-speed engine protocol is not directly comparable to the Aalto MU323DGSC three-cylinder four-stroke testbench.
audit_notes: The architecture combines detection, clustering, classification and prognostics instead of reporting only accuracy.
Important benchmark comparator for separating detection false positives, fault classification, RUL error and predictive uncertainty.

baselines.title: Literature Review Analysis: Fault Diagnostics of Marine Engines
baselines.data_domain: Scopus literature corpus covering 2015-2026, including marine diesel engines, marine gas turbines and closely related combustion-engine subsystems.
baselines.task: Systematic synthesis of diagnostic methods, monitored subsystems, data sources, validation practices and research gaps.

reported_metrics.context: Initial title extraction reported by the review.
Final refined corpus of papers directly related to marine-engine diagnostics.
Additional scope-adjacent papers retained separately from the core corpus.

baselines.split_protocol: Scopus-based literature search and title/abstract/keyword screening; the review organizes literature into seven methodological areas including model/simulation, signal processing, transferability, predictive diagnosis, reliability/maintenance, lubrication/wear and combustion/emissions.
reported_limitations: Literature screening is not a controlled model benchmark and its paper counts are not model-performance scores.
The review identifies limited long-term shipboard validation and lack of reusable public benchmark datasets as persistent gaps.
Paper counts must not be interpreted as a prevalence or fleet-failure distribution.

baselines.title: Fault diagnosis of marine diesel engine via control-aware domain-adversarial network: A control-diagnosis collaboration perspective
baselines.data_domain: Thermodynamic marine-engine simulation with fault diagnosis across maneuvering-regime distributions; no real-engine validation. Dataset is stated to be available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.
baselines.task: Control-aware injector-system fault diagnosis combining controller/control-signal features with physical state-signal features using control-generated feature weights and multi-class maneuvering-regime domain discrimination.

reported_metrics.context: The accessible abstract explicitly states experiments use simulation data from a thermodynamic model and that real-engine validation is absent. This is a scope fact, not a performance score.
Authors report stronger robustness than mainstream methods when control sensors drop out; exact quantitative effect and full dropout protocol require full-paper reproduction.

baselines.split_protocol: Simulation-only evaluation using a thermodynamic engine model and maneuvering-regime distributions. The accessible abstract does not disclose enough detail to reconstruct the exact split, class balance, sample independence, control-channel dropout distributions or model compute. Recover these from the full article and author-accessible data before reproduction.
reported_limitations: No real-engine validation is reported; do not describe the paper as physical test-bench or vessel validation.
The abstract's qualitative dropout robustness claim is not a quantified, independently reproduced metric.
Control-channel semantics, timing, controller-mode availability and command/feedback distinctions require full-methods audit.
Dataset available from corresponding author upon reasonable request; access and license are not established here.
audit_notes: Important architecture lead: distinguish control intent, actuator/controller state and physical plant response rather than treating all variables as generic features.

Compare state-only, control-only, naive fusion, gated fusion, control-aware multi-class regime adaptation and physics/rule-based command-response residual baselines under matched task/model/data budgets.

Aalto's accessible metadata does not establish that controller setpoints, governor outputs, actuator feedback or controller-mode signals are included; do not assume the dataset supports this benchmark before the payload and variable dictionary are inspected.
